name: Holly
seo_title: Holly Christmas Events for Kids 2026: 3 Events, 2 Free
seo_desc: Christmas events for kids in Holly, Michigan for 2026: 3 family events, 2 free, with dates, times and addresses checked on each host's site.
lede: Holly does Christmas Victorian style, with a lighted parade, three weekends of Dickens Festival streets and a light trail at the Michigan Renaissance Festival grounds.
celebrates: Holly's season centers on the Holly Dickens Festival, which presents the village's historic Battle Alley and Downtown Holly as a 19th century London street. The 2026 festival opens with the Dickens Lighted Parade and tree lighting on Friday, November 27, then runs three weekends of caroling, costumed characters, Tiny Tim's Santa Tent, live street performances and holiday shopping, with free admission for all ages. Just outside the village, the Michigan Renaissance Festival grounds host HollyDazzle, a lighted trail with Santa and a train, on select nights through December 31.
lastyear: The 2026 Holly Dickens Festival is billed as the 53rd annual, so last year's festival was the 52nd and followed the same pattern of early winter weekends in Downtown Holly. The festival's own site says it has run for 53 years, presented in partnership with Main Street Holly and Financial Plus Credit Union, with parking from Holly Area Schools and transportation from the Western Oakland Transportation Authority.
facts: The festival calls itself the oldest longest-running Dickens festival in the United States. Holly's Battle Alley earned its nickname more than 100 years ago because of the disputes settled there, and the festival site says temperance activist Carrie Nation once visited and smashed whiskey bottles with an ax. In 1838 Holly became the last township in Oakland County, and in 1865 the Village of Holly was incorporated.
trains: Holly grew up around railroads. The festival site says the Detroit, Milwaukee and Pontiac Railroad reached Holly in 1855 and that Holly became the first railroad junction in the state, with the Flint and Holly Railroad opening in 1864. Today HollyDazzle at the Michigan Renaissance Festival grounds includes a HollyDazzle train ride. Amtrak's Wolverine route serves Royal Oak and Troy, the closest stations for Oakland County families.
traditions: A parade and tree lighting on the Friday that opens the festival.
Three weekends of Victorian street scenes in Downtown Holly.
Historic alley at the heart of the festival.
A lighted outdoor trail with Santa and a train.
kidfact: Holly was the first railroad junction in Michigan, and kids can ride the HollyDazzle train today.
faq: With the Holly Dickens Festival, a Victorian themed street festival in Downtown Holly with a lighted parade, carolers, costumed characters and Tiny Tim's Santa Tent. HollyDazzle at the Michigan Renaissance Festival grounds adds a lighted trail with Santa and a train on select nights. Admission to the Dickens Festival is free for all ages.
Is the Holly Dickens Festival free?

Yes. The festival says admission is free for all ages. Some extras, such as the Victorian Tea and Tidings morning and the Run Like the Dickens race, are separate paid events, and the tea is listed as sold out.

Battle Alley is the historic alley in Downtown Holly at the heart of the festival. It earned its nickname more than 100 years ago because of the disputes settled there, according to the festival's site.
Can kids ride a train in Holly?
HollyDazzle at 12600 Dixie Highway includes a HollyDazzle train ride. Tickets are sold through Etix, and kids 4 and under are free.
Where do I park for the Dickens Festival?
Holly Area Schools provides parking at the Sherman Campus and Holly Elementary School, and the Western Oakland Transportation Authority provides transportation, according to the festival.
